chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Guitar or bass with piano; doubts about soloing
summary: Helen and Stanley Dance discuss piano-bass duos and cabaret licenses; Greene says he was not ready to solo then.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You had to be the drummer, huh? You had to watch the beat?
Yeah, I mean, like -- I guess that was it. Because, we didn't have any drummer at all. There was just, you know --
Well, we've been wondering -- you know, trying to think what the effect of the sound of that was like. Because as you know, some places in New York now have piano and bass.
Well, I can see that.
Yeah, but you can't really hear the bass. You know, like down in the Cookery. There's such a clatter of dishes and everything.
Oh yeah. Uh huh.
About the bass -- I mean I was just wondering if the guitar -- why the guitar couldn't be used just as effectively, because the guitar can come up and take a solo.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
I mean, you know most basses once, we were in the Hickory House, every number had 2 chorus for the bass, he said, 'its just like a commercial on TV.' Duke said to me
Yeah, but the bass, I think, is walking chords.
Yeah, but that's fine if it's really audible, but when you just have a piano and a bass.
Yeah. I understand you Stanley, but I just think the reason they do it is because the bass player can walk the chords more effectively probably than the guitar.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
Yeah. But you see, that's what they've got in places where they're not allowed to have drums.
Mm hmm.
Yeah.
Are there a lot of places where they're not allowed to have drums?
No. There's the cabaret license doesn't allow them to have drums, so they have piano and bass.
Oh, really?
Yeah. That's why they have those.
Well, Freddie, I can see guitar sounding pretty with piano. I mean, that's one of the things about the guitar is you kind of hear it.
Yeah.
And, I mean, so I can see it being pretty with piano.
Yeah. But, as I say, in the beginning, I kind of wondered, you know. But I stayed a long time, I mean, you know -- things went along fine.
Yeah. Well, you were probably a little worried about your own ability to fulfill your role.
Right. Right. Willie Gant striding...
Yeah. Yeah.
"How am I going to handle this situation?"
Yeah, but see, it was wonderful for you.
But you didn't ever sort of really want to be a soloist?
No. Not then. Because I didn't know the guitar well enough, you see?
Yeah.
No. Well, I mean, another case was when Al Casey was with where he was playing rhythm guitar, and then, you said, emerged as a soloist, too, chord style.
